text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- Arab parties condemn Iran's holding of Iraqi POWs.
- Iraq's representative to Islamic conference in Islamabad explains the dubious intentions behind the keeping of sanctions on Iraq.
- Toy pistol inflicts fear in the hearts of coward Zionists in Tel Aviv.
- Culture and Information Minister Hamed Youssef Hummadi receives head of U.N. Development Programme (UNDP) in Iraq.
- Meetings continue in Tikrit to discuss celebrations marking President Saddam Hussein birthday on April 28.
- Week of Indian cinema starts in Iraq.
- Iraq's envoy Abdul-Amir al-Anbari asks Japan to exert efforts to end sanctions on Iraq.
- Sudan contains aggression from Uganda.
- Israel suspends peace talks.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Article attacks Iran for holding Iraqi POWs and urges world public opinion to pressure Tehran to free them.
THAWRA
- Editorial on how to reduce expenditure and boost revenues in line with Saddam's directives.
- Commentary on Washington's policy of double standards and what Arab countries need to do to thwart it.
- Article exposes Tehran's dubious relations with its neighbours.
- Article on what Iraq needs to do to catch up with advances in multimedia technologies.
- Commentary on how to improve relations with countries neighbouring Iraq.
- Badiya land transport company prepares more than 600 trucks to take part in the transport of humanitarian goods inside Iraq.
JUMHOURIYA
- Iraq has provided information on 300 prisoners from countries which committed aggression on it in 1991.
- Editorial lambasts Van der Stoel, a special rapporteur of the Geneva-based U.N. Human Rights Commission for saying thousands of Iraqis were being killed or captured in Iraq without trial.
- Expansion in Iraqi-Pakistani bilateral ties.
- Central bank governor says deposits in Iraqi banks surged in the past year.
